title: The module system (JPMS): `module-info` and strong encapsulation

videos.script: Since lesson 14, public has meant anybody, anywhere. This lesson adds a wall above the package. {{module}} A module is a named group of packages, and one file, module-info, says which of them the rest of the world may see. {{refused}} A package the module does not export is not there for anyone outside it. The compiler says it does not exist. {{reflection}} Reflection stops at the same wall, and the JDK built that wall around itself. {{jlink}} Then a second use of modules. A tool reads what every module requires and builds a Java runtime with only those. Sixty megabytes instead of three hundred. {{honest}} And last, the honest part. Most Java applications have no module-info at all, and the lesson says why. By the end, you can read the module error that every Java developer meets, whether or not they ever write a module.
